bodies.thread:
Anthropic agreed to pay at least $1.5 billion plus interest to settle a class-action lawsuit over using pirated books for AI training.

The settlement payout works out to approximately $3,000 per book or work.

This is a notable discount compared to the maximum allowed penalty of $150,000 per book for copyright infringement.

Anthropic stated that the specific digital copies involved in this settlement were not used to train its commercially released AI models.

It appears legal in the USA to buy physical books, scan them, and train AI on that content under fair use.

Beyond legal battles, technical progress continues as the Kimi-K2-Instruct-0905 model now features 256,000 tokens.

This model uses 1 trillion parameters in a mixture-of-experts configuration with 384 experts, 32B activated parameters and 8 selected experts per token.

Better image retrieval performance can come from embedding highly opinionated summaries of images rather than using CLIP embeddings.

The legal landscape for AI training is shifting through settlements and court interpretations while technical challenges in data modeling remain.
